chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from al-Amraki ibn Ali, from Ali ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him), from his brother Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon both of them), who said:

I asked him about a group of people who pronounced the takbir (saying 'Allahu Akbar') for a funeral prayer either once or twice, and then another [takbir] was placed with it [i.e., they continued to a third or fourth]; how should they act? He said: 'If they wish, they may leave the first [takbir] until they finish the takbir for the last [one]; and if they wish, they may raise [continue from] the first one so as to complete what remained for the last one. All of that is permissible.'

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: There is no harm with it / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: How should one complete the funeral prayer takbirs if they missed one or combined them?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam Musa al-Kazim (AS) highlights the juristic flexibility (rukhsah) in the sequence of takbirs during Salat al-Janazah, addressing the practical issue of congregational synchronization. It establishes that whether worshippers restart the count for the missed takbir or integrate it into the subsequent sequence, both approaches are legally sound, reflecting the Shia emphasis on ease in ritual practice. This ruling is foundational in the *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* for resolving minor discrepancies in congregational prayer mechanics.
